own_solution.law: Ideal transformer Vs = Vp/4; bridge rectifier with two diodes of 0.7 V in the path: v = Vm|sin wt| - 1.4 V when Vm|sin wt| > 1.4 V, else 0; average = (1/pi)[2 Vm cos(th0) - 1.4 (pi - 2 th0)], th0 = asin(1.4/Vm)
assumptions: constant-drop ideal-switch diodes, two in series in each half-cycle
230 V rms is the actual (nominal) mains voltage

notes: Base: Vs = 57.5 V rms, Vm = 81.3173 V; th0 = asin(0.0172164) = 0.0172173 rad; 2Vm cos th0 = 162.6105; 1.4(pi - 2th0) = 4.3500; average = 158.2604/pi = 50.376 V. With 244 V rms: Vs = 61 V, Vm = 86.2670 V, th0 = 0.0162294, 2Vm cos th0 = 172.5113, 1.4(pi - 2th0) = 4.3528, average = 168.1586/pi = 53.527 V. Load resistance enters the current but cancels from the voltage with ideal constant-drop diodes (C). Lamp and earlier-run sentences have no path (D). T4891 ('14 V above its nominal value when the load voltage was measured') reads the stated 230 V rms as the nominal value; this is the usual reading of a mains rating, so I do not treat it as a contradiction, though the problem does not say 'nominal' explicitly. Number check: all 14 V sentences agree; both load sentences say 47 ohm; TAC9C and T644B are numeral-free.
